_comment: BOM (Bill of Materials) template for a Windows package. One file per bundle, generated by the packaging workflow into dist/BOM.json and shipped next to the setup (also validated by the iscc manifest gate). EVERY component of the bundle MUST appear here with an exact version/source/date, so a stale piece can FAIL the build instead of shipping silently. Copy this file, fill it in, and keep it in the repo as the record of what each release contains.

qt.source: official Qt release tarballs, https://download.qt.io/archive/qt/5.15/5.15.19/submodules/ (no git: the kde/5.15 branch on invent.kde.org requires an account and github.com/qt does not carry it)
qt.configure: <the exact flag string recorded by tools/build_qt_win64.ps1>
qt.sdk: <10.0.26100.0 (x64) | 10.0.19041.0 (x86: pinned, the newest SDK pulls W8+/W10 symbols)>
qt.build_time_openssl: <1.1.1w: DEVELOPMENT files only, needed by configure because of -openssl-runtime. No OpenSSL binary is shipped from the Qt build.>

openssl.version: <1.1.1w for the current bundles; moves to 3.5 LTS only after Qt >= 5.15.8 (see BUILD_QT_WINDOWS.md)>
openssl.source: https://slproweb.com (Light installer, extracted) - same source the workflow uses today

policy.refresh: Qt: only when a new 5.15 LTS patch is published on download.qt.io (the SHA256 pins have to be updated in the same commit). FFmpeg i686: re-run the recipe on a new 9.0.x/9.1. mpv: rolling dev build, pinned by tag -> needs its own refresh policy. OpenSSL: fastest cadence (~monthly patches), track the LTS line (currently 1.1.1w; the move to 3.5 is a separate, staged change).
policy.gate: The packaging workflow MUST read this file and FAIL when a component version does not match the expected pin (today the $need gate only checks that files EXIST, not their version).
